title: Office of Rural Affairs Enhancement Act
official_title: To amend the Small Business Act to clarify the responsibilities of the Office of Rural Affairs of the Small Business Administration, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Received in the Senate on December 2, 2025 and placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders (Calendar No. 282). Sponsored by a Democratic member with three cosponsors; referred in the House to the Committee on Small Business.
summary: Amends section 26 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 653) to clarify the Office of Rural Affairs (ORA) of the Small Business Administration. The Office is to be administered by an Assistant Administrator who is an employee in the competitive service and who must have education, professional experience, or knowledge of rural affairs and small business issues, as well as experience providing development assistance to rural small business concerns. The bill rewrites the duties in subsection (c) — replacing references to "small business concerns located in rural areas" with "rural small business concerns," changing "provide information" to "promote" the policies and programs of SBA and other federal agencies, updating the cross-reference from the United States Tourism and Travel Administration to the National Travel and Tourism Office of the Department of Commerce, and adding a new duty to host webinars and outreach events. New subsection (d) requires the Assistant Administrator to host webinars and outreach events across regions and to invite district-office representatives, resource partners, and Federal/State agencies. New subsection (e) requires the Administrator to submit annual reports (first due 180 days after enactment of the subsection) to the House Small Business Committee and the Senate Small Business and Entrepreneurship Committee, and make them publicly available, covering operational details, activities under subsection (c), number of webinars/events, an analysis of SBA lending programs' service to rural small businesses, and information gathered from outreach. New subsection (f) defines "Assistant Administrator," "resource partners" (small business development centers, women's business centers under section 29, SCORE chapters under section 8(b)(1)(B), and Veteran Business Outreach Centers under section 32), and "rural small business concern" (a small business concern in a rural area as defined in section 7(b)(16)).
brief: Restructures the Office of Rural Affairs at SBA — sets qualifications for a competitive-service Assistant Administrator, rewrites the Office's duties, requires nationwide webinars and outreach events, and adds an annual public report to the House and Senate small business committees.

top_lines.headline: Competitive-Service Assistant Administrator
subs: Office of Rural Affairs to be administered by an Assistant Administrator who is an employee in the competitive service
Must have education, professional experience, or knowledge of rural affairs and issues relating to small business concerns
Must have experience providing development assistance to rural small business concerns

top_lines.headline: Rewritten Office Duties
subs: "Small business concerns located in rural areas" replaced with "rural small business concerns" throughout paragraph (1)
In paragraph (3), "provide information" changed to "promote" the policies and programs of SBA and other federal agencies for assisting rural small business concerns
In paragraph (5), reference updated from the United States Tourism and Travel Administration to the National Travel and Tourism Office of the Department of Commerce
New paragraph (6) added: host webinars and outreach events for rural small business concerns as described in subsection (d)

top_lines.headline: New Outreach Duties
subs: Assistant Administrator must host webinars and outreach events in various regions of the United States for rural small business concerns
Must invite representatives from SBA district offices, resource partners, Federal and State agencies, and other interested persons

top_lines.headline: Annual Public Report
subs: First report due 180 days after enactment of subsection (e); annually thereafter
Submitted to the House Small Business Committee and the Senate Small Business and Entrepreneurship Committee, and made publicly available on an SBA website

Must include operational details (Assistant Administrator's name, Office budget, staffing), summary of subsection (c) activities, webinar/event counts, an analysis of SBA lending programs' service to rural small business concerns, and information gathered from outreach

items.main: Names the Act the "Office of Rural Affairs Enhancement Act."
items.detail: Short-title section only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Office of Rural Affairs of the Small Business Administration

items.main: Amends section 26 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 653), subsection (b), to require the Office to be administered by an Assistant Administrator who is an employee in the competitive service, and who has education/professional experience or knowledge of rural affairs and small business issues, plus experience providing development assistance to rural small business concerns.
items.detail: Paragraph (1) sets the appointment as a competitive-service position; paragraph (2) sets the qualifications.

items.main: Amends subsection (c) — changes references from "small business concerns located in rural areas" to "rural small business concerns," changes "provide information" to "promote" the policies and programs of SBA and other federal agencies, updates the reference from the United States Tourism and Travel Administration to the National Travel and Tourism Office of the Department of Commerce, and adds new paragraph (6) requiring the Office to host webinars and outreach events as described in subsection (d).
items.detail: Multiple striking-and-inserting amendments across paragraphs (1), (3), (4), and (5); paragraph (6) is the added item.

items.main: Adds new subsection (d) requiring the Assistant Administrator to host webinars and outreach events in various regions of the United States for rural small business concerns, and to invite representatives from SBA district offices, resource partners, Federal and State agencies, and other interested persons.
items.detail: Subsection (d) implements the new paragraph (6) duty added to subsection (c).

items.main: Adds new subsection (e) requiring the Administrator to submit annual reports to the House Committee on Small Business and the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship, and make each report publicly available on an SBA website. Reports must include operational details of the Office (Assistant Administrator's name, Office budget, number of full-time employees), a summary of subsection (c) activities, the number of webinars and outreach events, an analysis of SBA lending programs' service to rural small business concerns, and information gathered from outreach events.
items.detail: First report due not later than 180 days after enactment of subsection (e); annually thereafter.

items.main: Adds new subsection (f) definitions: "Assistant Administrator" (of the Office of Rural Affairs, appointed under subsection (b)); "resource partners" (small business development centers, women's business centers under section 29, SCORE chapters established under section 8(b)(1)(B), and Veteran Business Outreach Centers under section 32); "rural small business concern" (a small business concern located in a rural area as defined in section 7(b)(16)).

gaps: The bill does not authorize additional funding to carry out the outreach or reporting requirements.
The bill does not specify the frequency of webinars or a minimum number of regions to be covered.
The bill does not describe consequences if the Administrator fails to meet the report deadlines.
The bill does not modify SBA lending program terms — only the reporting analysis of those programs' rural service.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Goodlander
featured_quotes.text: H.R. 4549 is a bill that will deliver a fair deal for America's rural small businesses and entrepreneurs by cutting red tape, delivering access to key Federal resources, and ensuring experienced and accountable representation and leadership within our government. It is a bill that will ensure the voices of rural America aren't just heard but are truly prioritized within our government. Running a small business is really an act of faith.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Cisneros
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, I will, once again, thank my colleagues, Ms. Goodlander, Mr. Wied, and Mr. Golden, for their bipartisan efforts to pass this legislation. By strengthening the Office of Rural Affairs, we can ensure all small businesses have adequate access to the resources at their disposal.
